summary: Portfolio page timeouts originate in portfolio-service, not the api-gateway. At 09:52 a cost-optimisation config change (cfg-2207, infra-automation) cut portfolio-service's datasource pool max_size from 50 to 5. The pool immediately saturated (total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting 25-57), and requests could not acquire a JDBC connection within 3000ms, producing errors that surfaced as gateway p99 >4s and 504s. The suspected gateway HTTP/2 upgrade (dep-5220, 08:00) is contradicted: onset was 09:45/09:53, ~1h45m after deploy; order-service also received the h2 change but is unaffected; and the gateway itself has flat CPU/request rate. ledger-db is healthy. The only change matching onset is the pool config change.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Config change cfg-2207 shrunk portfolio-service DB pool 50→5, causing pool exhaustion and upstream timeouts
ranked_hypotheses.statement: An automated cost-optimisation config change (cfg-2207, 09:52) reduced portfolio-service's HikariCP datasource max_size from 50 to 5. With normal request rate (~560 req/s) the 5-connection pool saturated immediately (total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting 25-57); connections were held for the full 3000ms acquire timeout, so requests queued and failed, portfolio-service p99 rose to ~4.2s, and the api-gateway surfaced these as upstream timeouts/504s (perceived as portfolio page timeout).

causal_chain.claim: pool shrinks and saturates (db_pool_in_use pins at 5, total=5 active=5 idle=0 waiting>0)
requests fail to acquire a connection within 3000ms, portfolio p99 → ~4.2s
gateway reports upstream timeout portfolio-service /v1/portfolio/holdings -> 504, p99 >4s

assumptions: The 09:52 config change took effect without a restart, so the pool resized in place (consistent with F8 dropping at the 09:45/10:00 buckets).

ranked_hypotheses.title: api-gateway HTTP/2 upgrade (dep-5220) to upstreams broke portfolio-service calls
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The suspected cause: dep-5220 (08:00, 'enable HTTP/2 to upstreams' for portfolio-service and order-service) introduced an incompatibility or protocol-handling fault causing portfolio timeouts.

causal_chain.claim: gateway deploy enables h2 to portfolio-service at 08:00
h2 causes portfolio calls to time out

ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Onset is ~1h45m AFTER the deploy (09:45/09:53 vs 08:00) and the failure aligns to the 09:52 config change instead (F7). order-service received the identical h2 change and is completely unaffected (F12), and the gateway itself shows no saturation or internal errors (F14, F3). Portfolio errors are explicit JDBC/Hikari pool exhaustion, not protocol errors (F5).

ranked_hypotheses.title: ledger-db / shared datastore degradation slowed portfolio queries
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A ledger-db infrastructure problem (failover, IOPS throttle) made portfolio queries slow, exhausting connections.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: ledger-db cpu (~30%), slow_queries (~1/min) and connections are all flat/healthy; connections_active even fell (F13). Failures are client-side pool exhaustion (total=5), and the pool shrank rather than being blocked by a slow DB (F5, F8).

facts.statement: api-gateway p99 jumped from ~210ms to ~4.3s at the 09:45-10:00 window; error rate rose from 0.2% to ~7.2%.
Gateway logs show only upstream timeouts to portfolio-service returning 504, no gateway-internal faults.
portfolio-service p99 rose in lockstep with the gateway; its errors are JDBC connection-acquire failures and HikariPool exhaustion (total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting up to 57).
A config change cfg-2207 changed portfolio-service db.pool.max_size from 50 to 5 at 09:52:00.
portfolio-service log shows the config applied at 09:52:13 and the first connection failure at 09:53:19.
portfolio-service db_pool_in_use dropped from ~12 to exactly 5 after the change.
portfolio-service request rate and CPU are flat; no traffic or CPU trigger.
The only deployment was api-gateway dep-5220 at 08:00 enabling HTTP/2 to portfolio-service AND order-service.
order-service (identical h2 change) is completely unaffected; gateway CPU/request-rate flat.
ledger-db metrics are healthy; no datastore-side fault.

assumptions: cfg-2207 took effect in place without a restart (F8 shows the pool dropping precisely at the change, consistent with in-place resize).
The gateway 504s are the downstream symptom of portfolio-service failures, not an independent gateway fault (supported by F3, F5).

timeline.event: api-gateway dep-5220 (v9.3.0) deployed, enabling HTTP/2 to portfolio-service and order-service. No latency impact (p99 stays ~210ms for ~1h45m).
Config change cfg-2207 applies cost-optimisation profile: portfolio-service db.pool.max_size 50 -> 5.
portfolio-service logs 'config change cfg-2207 applied: db.pool.max_size=5'.
First 'could not acquire JDBC connection within 3000ms' error in portfolio-service.
Incident INC-002 reported (portfolio page timing out, gateway p99 high).
portfolio-service db_pool_in_use pins at 5.0; gateway/portfolio p99 plateau ~4.3s.

recommended_actions.action: Immediately revert cfg-2207: restore portfolio-service db.pool.max_size to 50 (or validate a correctly-sized value) and confirm pool recovery.
recommended_actions.rationale: The pool shrink is the direct cause; restoring pool size should clear the exhaustion and recover p99.

recommended_actions.action: Do NOT roll back gateway dep-5220 as the primary remediation; keep it in place unless independent evidence emerges.
recommended_actions.rationale: The h2 upgrade deploy predates onset by ~1h45m, is flat on order-service, and the gateway is not saturated — rolling it back would not fix the fault and adds risk.

recommended_actions.action: Add a guardrail/validation on datasource pool-size changes (minimum bound and canary) before infra-automation applies cost-optimisation profiles.
recommended_actions.rationale: Automated config overrode the pool to an unsafe value, mirroring HIST-115.

recommended_actions.action: Add alerting on Hikari pool saturation (active==total, waiting>0) and on client-side connection-acquire failures, distinct from generic 5xx.
recommended_actions.rationale: The exhaustion was visible in metrics/logs before the user-facing report and could have been detected faster.

recommended_actions.action: Audit other services for the same 'small' cost-optimisation profile being applied to datasources.
recommended_actions.rationale: Same automation could have silently shrunk pools elsewhere.

data_gaps: No confirmation of the fix outcome: we only have data through 11:59; cannot verify recovery after reverting cfg-2207.
Exact mechanism of the pool resize (whether HikariCP resized in place or on refresh) is inferred from the metric step, not directly logged.
No per-endpoint breakdown confirming that only /v1/portfolio/* paths on portfolio-service hit the DB pool, though all observed failures are on /v1/portfolio/holdings.

findings.statement: api-gateway p99 latency was ~205-214ms until 09:30, then jumped to 2147ms avg at the 09:45 bucket and plateaued at ~4300ms from 10:00 onward.
api-gateway error rate rose from ~0.2% to 3.03% in the 09:45 bucket and ~7.2% thereafter (504s).
Gateway logs are WARN-only and show 'upstream timeout portfolio-service GET /v1/portfolio/holdings -> 504' from 09:53:53 onward (252 occurrences); no gateway-internal errors.
portfolio-service p99 latency rose identically: ~180ms until 09:30, 2079ms at 09:45, ~4180ms from 10:00.

portfolio-service errors are dominated by JDBC connection-acquire failures and Hikari pool exhaustion: 'could not acquire JDBC connection within 3000ms' (270x) and 'HikariPool-1 - Connection is not available ... (total=5, active=5, idle=0' (233x), first seen 09:53:19.

findings.statement: A config change cfg-2207 on portfolio-service changed db.pool.max_size from 50 to 5 at 09:52:00Z, author infra-automation, description 'Apply cost-optimisation profile small'.

findings.statement: portfolio-service db_pool_in_use was steady ~12 (max 13.3) until 09:30, dropped to 8.62 at 09:45 and then pinned at exactly 5.0 for every bucket from 10:00 onward.
portfolio-service request rate is flat (~560 req/s) across the window; no traffic surge triggered the failure.
portfolio-service cpu_pct is flat at ~36% throughout, ruling out CPU saturation.

The only deployment in the window is dep-5220 on api-gateway (v9.3.0, 08:00, 'enable HTTP/2 to upstreams', 'upstream protocol h2 for portfolio-service and order-service'), status live, not rolled back.

refs.quote: upstream protocol h2 for portfolio-service and order-service

findings.statement: order-service, which also received the h2 upstream change, has flat error_rate (~0.2%) and flat p99 (~150ms) throughout the incident window.
ledger-db is healthy: cpu_pct flat ~30%, slow_queries_per_min flat ~1, connections_active slightly LOWER (~55 vs ~62), no failover or IOPS anomaly.
api-gateway cpu_pct (~42%) and request_rate (~1246 req/s) are flat across the window; the gateway is not saturated.
market-data-service p99/error-rate are flat across the window (dependency of portfolio-service is not the fault).
There were no portfolio-service deployments in the window (count 0).
Past incident HIST-115 is the same pattern: 'Datasource pool size overridden by a wrong environment profile', category config_change.
